settings.headlineLabel: Alien visitors + Iron Age lens = Fair Folk
settings.headline: What if the Fey were alien scientists studying us?
settings.body:
Out of the fairy ring comes a beautiful girl. She looks like Niamh, the village beauty. Almost.

You’re a young man in a small Celtic village in ancient Ireland. By day, you apprentice at the forge, shaping iron tools with the village smith. By night, you listen to your granny’s old stories of the Aos Sí or Fair Folk: Hollow hills, wandering lights, Red Caps, the Wild Hunt, and doors to the Otherworld. Granny swears the old stories were not always old. She says the lights in the hills began when she was twenty-three winters old, and that villagefolk only started calling them fairy doors after the first people went missing. 

You don’t believe in any of it, of course. You believe in iron, in work, in things that can be held in the hand. Still, you do not wander into the hollow hills after dark. 

Niamh? You’re secretly in love with Niamh. Half the village is. Niamh is beautiful, unapproachable, kind, sharp-witted, perfect in an almost uncanny way with her fair hair, her soft skin, her symmetrical freckles. Who has symmetrical freckles? Niamh has.

Some villagers don’t like her. Some say she’s a witch. Your granny thinks she’s a changeling. But then again, Granny explains everything with the Fair Folk - missing livestock, distant lights in the dark, eerie sounds in the night, old Conroy vanishing into the woods. Superstitions. Children’s tales. 

Still, you do not wander into the hollow hills after dark. Until tonight.

It was the goat’s fault. He ran off; you were unable to catch him. How can a goat be that fast? Now you’re standing in a glade, under the pale moon. In the middle of the clearing, you see a perfect ring of mushrooms. Granny calls them fairy rings. Suddenly, the circle starts to glow in an eerie blue light - and out of thin air materialises a beautiful, naked girl, floating as if held by invisible hands. 

She looks like Niamh. 

But she is not Niamh. 

Who is she?
